full_text_en:
Guangxi Xineng Technology Co., Ltd. v. Guotai Junan Securities Co., Ltd. — dispute over entrusted asset management contract

Ruling Summary

Where an asset manager, acting in accordance with an asset management entrustment agreement, makes normal investment decisions based on commercial judgment in stock market securities transactions, so long as the manager has fulfilled the duty of good faith management and there is no clear fault, the manager shall not bear the consequences of trading losses.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2003) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 182

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Guangxi Xineng Technology Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 306, 3rd Floor, Keyuan Building, Keyuan Avenue, Nanning City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Wang Kai, Chairman of the Board of Directors.

Agent ad litem: Li Anhua, Attorney at Far East Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Guotai Junan Securities Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 618 Shangcheng Road, Pudong New Area, Shanghai City.

Legal Representative: Zhu Youyi, Chairman of the Board of Directors.

Agent ad litem: Li Zhonghua, employee of the company.

Agent ad litem: Chen Kai, Attorney at Beijing Tiantong Law Firm.

The Appellant, Guangxi Xineng Technology Co., Ltd., appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (No. 1 (2003) Hu Gao Min Er (Shang) Chu Zi) rendered by the Shanghai High People's Court in the case of dispute over the entrusted asset management contract with the Appellee, Guotai Junan Securities Co., Ltd. This Court formed a collegiate panel in accordance with the law, with Judge Ye Xiaoqing as the presiding judge, Acting Judge Chen Mingyan and Wang Chuang as members, and Court Clerk Yin Jing serving as recorder. The case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts:

On December 18, 2000, Party A, Guangxi Chuangzhi Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Chuangzhi Technology), the predecessor of Guangxi Xineng Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xineng Company), and Party B, Guotai Junan Securities Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guotai Junan Company), entered into a "Guotai Junan Securities Co., Ltd. Asset Management Entrustment Agreement with Guangxi Chuangzhi Technology Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as the "Asset Management Entrustment Agreement"). The main contents of the agreement were as follows: 1. Guotai Junan Company accepted the entrustment of Chuangzhi Technology to provide asset management services, with entrusted funds totaling RMB 100 million, and the entrustment period from December 20, 2000, to December 20, 2001. 2. Guotai Junan Company would open a dedicated capital account at Guotai Junan Company and its business departments based on the securities account provided by Chuangzhi Technology, and deposit the full amount of entrusted funds managed by Chuangzhi Technology into such dedicated capital account. The income and realized funds from various investments under the entrusted assets could only be operated within such dedicated capital account and could not be misappropriated. Chuangzhi Technology provided the shareholder account name for the Shenzhen Stock Exchange as "Chuangzhi Company," with shareholder number 63176363; and the shareholder account name for the Shanghai Stock Exchange as "Chuangzhi Company," with shareholder number B880601892. Chuangzhi Technology also designated that Guotai Junan Company conduct securities trading in two personal accounts: Fang Donglian (Shanghai stock code: 364776357, Shenzhen stock code: 22439602) and Wang Xinyou (Shanghai stock code: 364777337, Shenzhen stock code: 22439700). 3. Guotai Junan Company must act with due caution and diligence, apply professional knowledge and skills in its services, and take the safety and stable income of the entrusted assets as the asset management objective; if Guotai Junan Company fails to perform its duties resulting in losses to the entrusted assets of the entrusting party, it shall compensate for such losses, with the scope of compensation sufficient to cover the total amount of the entrusted assets. Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, Guotai Junan Company, under the securities account name designated by the principal, and without violating the interests of the principal, had the right to autonomously operate the purchase and sale of funds in the dedicated capital account and hold legally invested varieties in the lawful financial markets within China. However, it must not arrange any form of borrowing or other liability funds for the dedicated capital account. 4. Guotai Junan Company must realize all securities in the designated securities account before the termination of the entrustment period. Within five working days after the termination of the entrustment period, Guotai Junan Company should pay the ending balance of the entrusted assets to the principal after deducting the agreed management fee and performance compensation. 5. Guotai Junan Company should regularly (monthly, annually, and upon termination of the entrustment period) provide asset management reports to the principal during the entrustment period. 6. The parties agreed on the method of deducting management fees: when the annual yield was less than 7%, Guotai Junan Company would not charge a management fee; when the annual yield was below 10%, Guotai Junan Company would not deduct performance compensation; for the portion of the annual yield between 10% and 20%, Guotai Junan Company would charge a certain proportion of earnings, etc. 7. If Guotai Junan Company failed to pay the ending balance to the principal after the expiration of the agreed entrustment period, it would pay late payment penalty at a rate of 0.04% per day on the amount payable; if any party breached its obligations under the agreement and caused losses, the breaching party should pay the other party liquidated damages equal to 5% of the initial balance of the entrusted assets, and provide full and effective compensation to the other party. The parties also agreed on other matters. After the agreement was signed, Chuangzhi Technology, on December 20, 2000, remitted the entrusted funds of RMB 100 million to the account designated by Guotai Junan Company.

On September 19, 2001, with the approval of the administrative department for industry and commerce, the original "Guangxi Chuangzhi Technology Co., Ltd." was renamed "Guangxi Xineng Technology Co., Ltd."

On November 25, 2001, Guotai Junan Company and Xineng Company, after negotiation, reached an "Asset Management Entrustment Extension Agreement" (hereinafter referred to as the "Extension Agreement"). The agreement provided that Xineng Company would continue to entrust Guotai Junan Company to manage the entrusted assets in accordance with the terms of the original agreement, with the entrusted funds still being RMB 100 million, and the entrustment period extended to December 20, 2002. The rights and obligations of Chuangzhi Technology under the original agreement were assumed by the renamed Xineng Company. Guotai Junan Company agreed to pay Xineng Company entrusted investment income at 6% of the entrusted funds within one day after the expiration of the original agreement. During the extended entrustment period, the rights and obligations of the parties would still follow the provisions of the original agreement. Where the original agreement and the Extension Agreement were inconsistent, the provisions of the Extension Agreement would prevail.

After the Extension Agreement was signed, Guotai Junan Company paid Xineng Company the prior income of RMB 6 million as agreed. During the performance of the original agreement and the Extension Agreement, Guotai Junan Company did not provide asset management reports to Xineng Company on a regular basis as agreed. After the expiration of the entrustment period as agreed in the Extension Agreement, Guotai Junan Company did not realize the stocks in the securities account and also did not pay the account balance to the principal. Based on the stock transaction confirmation statements provided by Guotai Junan Company and verified by the court of first instance, as of December 20, 2002, the total stock market value (calculated at the closing price of the purchased stocks on that day) and the capital balance in Xineng Company's account amounted to RMB 80,698,548.97, resulting in a loss of RMB 19,301,451.03 in entrusted fund transactions.

On March 20, 2003, Xineng Company filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai High People's Court, requesting a judgment ordering Guotai Junan Company to return the principal of the entrusted management fund of RMB 100 million and late payment penalty of RMB 3.6 million, liquidated damages of RMB 5 million, and to bear the litigation costs.

During the proceedings of the first instance, on May 13, 2003, Guotai Junan Company voluntarily returned RMB 50 million to Xineng Company.

The court of first instance, after trial, held: Guotai Junan Company, as a comprehensive securities company approved by the competent authorities to engage in entrusted investment management business, has the business qualifications for entrusted investment management. The "Asset Management Entrustment Agreement" and the "Extension Agreement" signed between it and Xineng Company were the result of consultation between the two parties, representing their true intentions, and did not violate prohibitive provisions of laws or administrative regulations. Their agreements should be deemed valid. After accepting Xineng Company's entrustment, Guotai Junan Company should manage Xineng Company's entrusted funds comprehensively in accordance with the agreement. However, during the entrustment period, Guotai Junan Company did not fully perform its contractual obligations; it did not provide asset management reports to Xineng Company on time, violating the contractual duty to inform; after the expiration of the agreed entrustment period, it did not realize the securities in the designated securities account and return them to Xineng Company, and should bear liability for default on late payment. Xineng Company and Guotai Junan Company agreed on a compensation clause for losses in the Extension Agreement, which provided that if Guotai Junan Company failed to exercise due diligence and caution, it should compensate Xineng Company for losses of the fund principal. However, the precondition for the application of this clause was that Xineng Company must prove that Guotai Junan Company violated the duty of care and diligence as a manager. Therefore, without evidence proving that Guotai Junan Company violated the duty of a manager, Xineng Company's claim for compensation for the loss of fund principal based on this clause had no factual basis. In terms of entrusted securities trading itself, the principal should directly bear the trading risks and trading losses resulting from the transactions conducted by the agent, unless the agent had intentionally violated the principal's trading instructions and harmed the principal's interests; otherwise, the agent should not bear the consequences of trading losses. In this case, apart from partial breach of contract, Xineng Company had no evidence to prove that Guotai Junan Company had any conduct violating legal provisions during the securities trading process. The trading losses from stock operations also constituted normal market risk losses in the environment of a downturn in the stock market. In this respect, Guotai Junan Company had no clear fault, and it should not bear liability for losses arising from such trading. Guotai Junan Company should only be liable for returning the securities market value that should have been realized on the date of termination of the entrustment period, and calculate late payment penalty as agreed on that basis. Therefore, the court did not support Xineng Company's request for Guotai Junan Company to compensate for the loss of the entrusted fund principal; as for Guotai Junan Company's request to adjust the standard for late payment penalty, because the agreed standard was not improper and did not violate legal provisions, the court did not accept that defense. The court held that since the contract did not establish any precondition for Guotai Junan Company's obligation to regularly provide asset management reports to Xineng Company, it was an obligation that Guotai Junan Company should faithfully perform and also one of the independent rights enjoyed by Xineng Company. Even if Xineng Company could take proactive measures to obtain relevant asset management information, it could not exempt Guotai Junan Company from proactively performing this obligation. Although Guotai Junan Company's failure to provide reports did not cause losses to Xineng Company, the payment of liquidated damages and compensation for losses are not necessarily linked; Guotai Junan Company's omission caused Xineng Company's right to obtain reports to be unrealized. Therefore, the court supported Xineng Company's request for Guotai Junan Company to pay liquidated damages. Guotai Junan Company should bear liability for breach of contract in accordance with the contract and pay liquidated damages of RMB 5 million to Xineng Company. In summary, the Shanghai High People's Court, in accordance with Articles 60, 114(1), and 401 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment: 1. Guotai Junan Securities Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days of the effectiveness of this judgment, pay Guangxi Xineng Technology Co., Ltd. RMB 30,698,548.97 (of which the stock market value is calculated based on the closing price of the purchased stocks on the agreed payment date of December 20, 2002, minus the RMB 50 million already paid by Guotai Junan Company) and pay corresponding late payment penalty for overdue payment (from December 21, 2002, to May 13, 2003, based on RMB 80,698,548.97 at a rate of 0.04% per day; from May 14, 2003, to the date of effectiveness of this judgment, based on RMB 30,698,548.97 at a rate of 0.04% per day). 2. Guotai Junan Securities Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days of the effectiveness of this judgment, pay Guangxi Xineng Technology Co., Ltd. liquidated damages of RMB 5 million. 3. The remaining claims of Guangxi Xineng Technology Co., Ltd. are not supported. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 553,010 shall be borne by Guangxi Xineng Technology Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 82,951.5, and by Guotai Junan Securities Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 470,058.5.

Xineng Company, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the Shanghai High People's Court, appealed to this Court, arguing: 1. The court of first instance admitted stock transaction confirmation statements submitted beyond the time limit for evidence submission, violating the rules of evidence; 2. As seen from the stock transaction confirmation statements, Guotai Junan Company conducted two transactions of buying high and selling low, and selling low and buying high, which either transferred profits from Xineng Company's account or aimed to earn handling fees; at the expiration of the first year of entrusted asset management, it concealed losses and falsely reported profits, constituting securities fraud. The court of first instance failed to find that Guotai Junan Company had engaged in securities fraud, which was clearly inconsistent with the evidence; 3. Guotai Junan Company failed to fulfill its duty of diligence and caution. It requested the court to order the Appellee Guotai Junan Company to return its entrusted assets of RMB 50 million, pay late payment penalty at 0.04% per day as per the contract, and pay liquidated damages of RMB 5 million. In the second-instance trial, given that Guotai Junan Company voluntarily returned the principal of the entrusted assets of RMB 30.7 million to the Appellant Xineng Company, the Appellant changed its claim to request the court to order the Appellee Guotai Junan Company to return the entrusted assets of RMB 19.3 million, pay late payment penalty at 0.04% per day as per the contract, and pay liquidated damages of RMB 5 million.

The Appellee Guotai Junan Company argued in its defense: 1. Guotai Junan Company received the Notice of Evidence Submission on May 11 in the first instance, and subsequently submitted an application for extension to the court of first instance. Its submission of evidence complied with the rules of evidence; 2. Guotai Junan Company did not deceive Xineng Company, and Xineng Company's claim that Guotai Junan Company engaged in securities fraud had no factual basis; 3. There was no impropriety in the management of entrusted assets; the loss of entrusted assets was caused by the overall environment of the stock market downturn. Guotai Junan Company had timely notified and reported the status of assets to Xineng Company and should not bear liability for compensating investment losses. It requested the court to dismiss the appeal of Xineng Company.

In addition to confirming the facts found by the court of first instance, this Court also found the following during the second-instance trial: 1. The "Notice of Evidence Submission" of the court of first instance required the parties to submit evidence within 30 days of receiving the notice. Guotai Junan Company signed for the "Notice of Evidence Submission" on May 11, 2003. 2. On May 28, 2003, Guotai Junan Company submitted a "Application for Extension of Time for Evidence Submission" to the court of first instance, and submitted the stock transaction confirmation statements within the extended period. 3. On November 12, 2003, Guotai Junan Company voluntarily returned RMB 30.7 million to Xineng Company.

This Court holds: The dispute in this case concerns a relationship under an entrusted asset management contract with the objective of investment in the securities market. Guotai Junan Company, as a comprehensive securities company approved by the competent authorities to engage in entrusted investment management business, has the business qualifications for entrusted investment management. The "Asset Management Entrustment Agreement" and the "Extension Agreement" signed between it and Xineng Company represent the true intentions of the parties, do not violate prohibitive provisions of laws or administrative regulations, and should be deemed lawful and valid.

According to the facts found by this Court, Guotai Junan Company submitted an application for extension of time for evidence submission before the expiration of the time limit for evidence submission in the first instance, and the court of first instance also agreed to extend the time for submitting evidence. Guotai Junan Company submitted the stock transaction confirmation statements within the extended time limit, which did not exceed the time limit for evidence submission. Xineng Company waived its right to cross-examine the stock transaction confirmation statements in the first instance. Although in the second-instance trial it questioned the authenticity of the contents of the above confirmation statements, it could not provide counter-evidence to overturn the evidence submitted by Guotai Junan Company, and also waived its procedural right to request an appraisal or audit of the above evidence. Therefore, this Court confirms that the stock transaction confirmation statements can serve as evidence for finding the facts of this case, namely the balance of the entrusted assets at the termination of the "Asset Management Entrustment Agreement." The cross-examination activities of the court of first instance regarding the evidence in this case complied with the rules of evidence. Xineng Company's claim that the first-instance trial cross-examination violated the rules of evidence lacks factual basis, and this Court does not accept it.

The "Asset Management Entrustment Agreement" provided that Guotai Junan Company, without violating the interests of the principal, had the right to autonomously operate the purchase and sale of funds in the dedicated capital account and hold legally invested varieties in the lawful financial markets within China, but must not arrange any form of borrowing or other liability funds for the dedicated capital account. Xineng Company argued that Guotai Junan Company, in the asset management, conducted two transactions of buying high and selling low and selling low and buying high, thereby transferring profits from Xineng Company's account and fabricating income, constituting fraud against Xineng Company. However, Xineng Company has no evidence to prove that Guotai Junan Company engaged in conduct violating the law during the securities trading process, or that it had clear fault or transferred profits from Xineng Company's account. In the operation of stock market securities trading, Guotai Junan Company's normal investment conduct based on commercial judgment, even if it involved an error in investment judgment, does not constitute a basis for requiring it to bear compensation liability simply because its commercial judgment at the time was contrary to the subsequent factual development of the market, provided it fulfilled its duty as a manager with caution and diligence as agreed in the contract and did not have clear fault. Moreover, the trading losses from stock operations in this case also constituted normal risk losses in the downturn of the stock market. Therefore, in the context of a large volume of long-term stock trading, Xineng Company's claim that Guotai Junan Company violated its duty of good faith management and constituted fraud against Xineng Company based solely on two instances of buying high and selling low is clearly insufficient evidence. According to Article 1 of the Extension Agreement, Guotai Junan Company was to pay Xineng Company income at 6% of the capital principal. Xineng Company argued that Guotai Junan Company thereby fabricated income, constituting fraud against Xineng Company. However, since at the time of signing the Extension Agreement, the original agreement had not yet expired, and it was impossible to know the income at the expiry date at that time, Guotai Junan Company noted on the payment that the amount was a "prepaid" entrusted investment income payment. However, when signing, Xineng Company unilaterally crossed out the character "pre" (预). Subsequently, on the payment voucher for the RMB 6 million paid to Guotai Junan Company, the payment purpose was also noted as "pre-distribution of income." Accordingly, it can be determined that the RMB 6 million determined in the Extension Agreement was prepaid income, and Guotai Junan Company did not fabricate profits. Therefore, this Court does not support Xineng Company's ground of appeal that Guotai Junan Company bought high and sold low stocks, transferred profits from Xineng Company's account, fabricated income, thereby constituting fraud against Xineng Company, and should bear the corresponding consequences.

Article 6(2)(1) of the Asset Management Entrustment Agreement provides that Guotai Junan Securities Co., Ltd. shall "strictly comply with all the provisions of current laws and all the provisions of this Agreement, prudently and diligently perform asset management obligations, and ensure the safety and stable income of the entrusted assets; if losses are incurred to Party A's entrusted assets due to failure to perform such obligations, it shall compensate Party A for the losses of the entrusted assets, and the scope of compensation shall be limited to making up for the total amount of the entrusted assets." Item 4 provides that it shall "regularly provide asset management reports to Party A during the entrustment period (monthly, annually, and upon termination of the entrustment period)." It can be seen from the above that the parties distinguished in the entrustment agreement between the obligation of a prudent and diligent manager and the obligation to provide asset management reports. The obligation of Guotai Junan to submit asset management reports to Xineng Company does not fall within the scope of "prudently and diligently performing asset management" as agreed in Article 6(2)(1) of the agreement between the parties. The first-instance judgment found that the loss of Xineng Company's entrusted assets was a normal risk loss under a sluggish stock market environment and that Guotai Junan had no obvious fault in the process of entrusted management. Such finding is not improper. We do not support Xineng Technology's claim for ordering Guotai Junan to return all the entrusted funds.

Guotai Junan proactively returned RMB 30.70 million to Xineng Company on November 12, 2003. The above-repaid principal and corresponding late fees and interest shall be deducted in the execution of this case.

In summary, the court of first instance found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. In accordance with Article 153(1)(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, we hereby rule as follows:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 553,010 shall be executed according to the original judgment; the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 160,010 shall be borne by the appellant Guangxi Xineng Technology Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Ye Xiaoqing

Acting Judge: Chen Mingyan

Acting Judge: Wang Chuang

February 19, 2004

Clerk: Yin Jing
